players.product: Liquid cooling, power distribution units, enclosures and electrical connection/protection for AI data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results on the call: sales of $1.067 billion were up 42% year over year, with organic growth of 24%, 'well ahead of our guidance driven by stronger than forecasted data center sales'; acquisitions added $126 million (17 points). Adjusted operating income was $210 million (+33%) at a 19.7% return on sales, 'a bit lower than expected due to higher investments, incentive compensation, and mix'. Adjusted EPS $0.90 (+53%, above the high end of guidance); free cash flow $189 million (+26%). Infrastructure organic sales were up over 50% on data centers; Americas grew approximately 30%, Europe high single digits, Asia Pacific down. Second consecutive quarter above $1 billion in sales. Inflation was nearly $55 million, including more than $40 million of tariff impact, offset by price plus productivity.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 sales $1.067 billion (+42%, organic 24%); adjusted EPS $0.90 (+53%); return on sales 19.7%

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 segment performance: Systems Protection sales of $737 million increased 58% (acquisitions 23 points; organic 34% with all verticals growing and infrastructure up approximately 70% 'largely due to continued strength in data centers'); segment income $149 million (+49%) at a 20.3% return on sales, down 120 basis points on inflation, growth investments and recent acquisitions. Electrical Connections sales of $330 million increased 15% (organic 8%, EPG acquisition six points) with infrastructure up approximately 25%; segment income $91 million (+8%) at a 27.6% return on sales, down 180 basis points primarily on inflation.
quarterly_data.figure: Systems Protection $737 million (+58%, organic 34%, infrastructure approximately 70%); Electrical Connections $330 million (+15%, organic 8%)

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center business sized: management cited 'data center sales representing approximately $1 billion in 2025' (CEO: 2025 data-center revenue 'reached over a billion'), versus $600 million in 2024, with data centers growing over 50% for the year. Fastest growth is in liquid cooling and power, with cable management 'also growing very nicely'. The infrastructure vertical rose from 12% of sales at spin to 45% in 2025 and is expected to be 'well over half' of sales in 2026. Full-year 2025 sales were $3.9 billion (+30%, +13% organic), adjusted EPS +35%, and record free cash flow of $561 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Data center sales approximately $1 billion in 2025 vs $600 million in 2024; infrastructure 45% of sales

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and backlog: Q4 organic orders were up approximately 30%, 'primarily driven by large orders for the AI data center build-out'; excluding data centers, organic orders grew low double digits (after high single digits in Q3), and 'orders continue to look good through January'. Year-end backlog was 'triple what it was a year ago', primarily data center plus the newly acquired businesses supporting that vertical, with healthy backlog also in Electrical Connections and core Systems Protection; most of the backlog is through 2026, 'although there's some beyond that'. Data-center orders 'can be very lumpy' ('tremendous orders in Q3 and good orders in Q4'), and management expects continued large orders that will not be smooth through the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Organic orders up approximately 30% (ex-data-center low double digits); backlog triple year-ago

quarterly_data.signal: Initial FY2026 outlook: reported sales growth 15% to 18% and organic growth 10% to 13% (acquisitions approximately four points, FX a one-point tailwind); adjusted EPS $4 to $4.15 (growth of 20% to 24%); free cash flow conversion 90% to 95%; CapEx of approximately $130 million; incremental tariffs of approximately $80 million, largely in the first half, to be offset by price and productivity. Infrastructure is expected to grow approximately 20%, 'driven by AI data center CapEx acceleration', with power utilities, renewables and energy storage also growing; industrial mid-single digits, commercial resi low single digits. Q1 2026 guide: reported sales growth 34% to 36% (acquisitions approximately 15 points), organic 17% to 19%, adjusted EPS $0.90 to $0.93. The CFO called the full-year guide early ('We've entered a period of unprecedented growth'), noting it overlaps 20% organic and 50% EPS growth in 2025 and leaves flexibility to invest.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 organic growth 10% to 13%; adjusted EPS $4 to $4.15; CapEx of approximately $130 million; Q1 organic growth 17% to 19%

quarterly_data.signal: Liquid-cooling capacity build: in January nVent opened a new facility in Blaine, Minnesota 'to expand our liquid cooling capacity' — 'Production is online, and we are ramping quickly'; the CEO said it took 'just over a hundred days' from announcing the expansion and signing the lease to producing. 2025 CapEx of $93 million (up 26%) went to recent acquisitions and new capacity for data centers and power utilities. The rapid ramp brings inefficiencies ('we're ramping so quickly and having to train a lot of new people'), and first-half margins carry the new-capacity investments, carryover tariffs and the EPG acquisition, with the second half expected to be better.
quarterly_data.figure: Blaine, Minnesota liquid cooling facility opened in January; just over a hundred days from lease to production

quarterly_data.signal: New liquid-cooling products and NVIDIA road-map alignment: nVent showcased new scalable, modular liquid-cooling products at Supercompute that launch 'through Q1 and Q2', with customer reception 'very strong'. On a new CDU launching this year, the CEO said 'we've been working with NVIDIA, and we understand those technology road maps and those heat loads out to 2030', and 'what we can do with this new CDU we're launching would have taken two CDUs in the past'; nVent is 'working with all the chip manufacturers' to design higher heat loads into the portfolio. In 2025 nVent launched 86 new products, contributing approximately 10 points to sales growth, with new product vitality of 27%.
quarterly_data.figure: 86 new products in 2025 (approximately 10 points to sales growth); new CDU does the work of two; NVIDIA heat-load road maps out to 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Liquid-cooling penetration and competition: management said 'currently less than 30% of data centers have liquid cooling', which 'is going to grow significantly because of the heat loads and power densities' (an update was promised for the February 24 Investor Day). nVent has done liquid cooling 'for well over a decade', working with 'some large hyperscalers for a long time', and is 'several generations in'; it acknowledged 'a lot of new entrants' and expects liquid-cooling demand 'from hyperscalers to colos to enterprise', and eventually non-data-center applications.
quarterly_data.figure: less than 30% of data centers have liquid cooling

quarterly_data.signal: Power utilities: management sees 'solid growth and opportunity', mainly through T&D and 'in particular, sub' — substations 'whether that's for utilities or it's supporting data centers' — with pull-through of its integrated engineering building solutions; recent acquisitions are trending ahead of deal plan (the CEO confirmed an analyst's question). Power-utility orders were not as strong as data centers but are part of ex-data-center orders up low double digits.
